note: Commercially a clean fit and a clean miss on starting point. He is a consultant who owns his own business in talent advisory and contingent workforce management, which satisfies 'successful', and the $6,000 drew literally no resistance — 'All right. That's fine.' — which settles income more decisively than anything said on the other calls in this batch. Health is squarely the neglected area: three to four years without consistent training while the business, the moves between countries and two young children took everything. He is emphatically not gym-averse — a former Division 1 athlete who has trained in gyms since 16, uses kettlebells competently and is by his own account addicted to padel — so the exclusion does not bite on the attitude half. The miss is good-to-great: he says outright 'I need to lose a lot of weight' and is starting from three years of inactivity, which is rescue rather than refinement, and he explicitly disclaims the aspirational end state — 'I don't aim to look like Trevor... If my gut goes away, I consider myself extremely blessed.' The criterion the ICP does not contain is again the one that decides this case: bone-on-bone knee osteoarthritis after a four-ligament rupture. Third consecutive prospect in this batch where the clinical picture is the material fact and the stated ICP has nothing to say about it.
